title: Feedback lane architectures and mini proposals — Nov 2027
content:
TL;DR:
Collected ~210 raw requests from Q3–Q4 voice capture (support, sales calls, NPS comments). This doc synthesizes into 7 compact request lanes, each with a quick implementation sketch, risk flags, and the smallest possible experiment we can run to validate impact. Priority lanes recommended: 1) Predictive fallback routing for model variants, 2) Token cost fingerprinting per customer, 3) Prompt-set-driven quality alerts.

Context + sources:
- Data sources: support tickets (tagged 'model-behavior', 'latency'), field notes (sales call transcripts), in-product feedback widget, CS weekly capture spreadsheet (Q3–Q4 2027).
- Sampling note: ~30% of asks are edgecases (rare), 45% are friction/UX optimizations, 25% are ops/observability asks.
- Quick metrics: top reported pain = opaque cost spikes (47% of customers who filed tickets about cost), second = silent model degradations (35%).

Synthesis: high-level themes (how customers describe problem)
- “Why did my bill jump?” — need per-route, per-prompt, per-model cost visibility and anomaly detection.
- “Model suddenly hallucinated after rollout” — rollout-tracking, canary rollbacks, and regression alerts tied to evaluation prompts.
- “Latency is fine locally but spikes in production” — capacity and routing telemetry (region, tier, queue depth).
- “No clear guidance on when to quantize/optimize” — recommendations for quantization/size tradeoffs based on workload.
- “We need deterministic fallbacks” — predictable fallback behavior when primary model fails or is slow.

Request compendium (7 lanes) — each lane includes shorthand (impact/effort), sample customer quote, micro-proposal, minimal experiment:

1) Cost fingerprinting per-customer (Impact: H / Effort: M)
- Quote: "We saw a +40% token spend week after enabling chat mode — no idea why." — enterprise fintech
- Micro-proposal: Add token-level attribution: route -> model -> prompt template -> feature flag. Store cost metadata in daily digest per customer with 7-day moving baseline and anomaly score.
- Minimal experiment: Roll out a 10-account beta with a simple daily CSV export (no UI) and ask CS to validate whether it explains >70% of billing variance.
- Risk: data retention + PII; need to filter user content.

2) Predictive fallback routing (Impact: H / Effort: H)
- Quote: "When the large model timed out our app froze — we want fallback to cheaper smaller model automatically." — marketplace app
- Micro-proposal: Policy engine rule type: on-latency/timeout -> route to pinned model variant; include prediction window using recent latency quantiles per instance.
- Minimal experiment: Canary 5% traffic on non-critical route with a TTL-based fallback enabled; monitor error-rate and conversion metrics.
- Risk: different model might degrade quality — need quality guardrail (eval prompts).

3) Prompt-set quality alerts (Impact: M / Effort: M)
- Quote: "After a prompt tweak our summaries regressed for legal docs — why didn't we know?" — legal SaaS
- Micro-proposal: Allow customers to upload or point to small eval prompt sets; compute baseline metrics and trigger regression alerts when response-score drops beyond threshold.
- Minimal experiment: Offer to 3 customers as a free add-on, collect feedback on alert usefulness.
- Risk: customers won't curate good prompt sets; provide starter templates.

4) Cost-aware model recommendations (Impact: M / Effort: L)
- Quote: "We'd like a suggestion: same quality cheaper model for embeddings." — search team
- Micro-proposal: Light-weight recommender: given usage patterns (seq length, top-p, streaming), recommend model variant and expected savings. Attach a confidence band.
- Minimal experiment: Run offline for 50 customers, show potential savings in CSV, ask for opt-in trials.

5) Route-level latency heatmap and source attribution (Impact: M / Effort: M)
- Quote: "We see latency spikes but can't tell if it's network, kv-cache misses, or model warmup." — adtech customer
- Micro-proposal: Instrument route-level spans: ingress queue time, pairing latency, kv cache hit/miss, kernel stalls. Expose a simple heatmap in Console with 90/95/99 percentile bars.
- Minimal experiment: Instrument two routes for two customers for two weeks; share heatmap PDF with SRE and customers.

6) Quick rollback hooks for rollouts (Impact: H / Effort: M)
- Quote: "Canary failed silently; we had to manually revert and lost minutes." — enterprise platform
- Micro-proposal: Add a rollback API to Console and CLI to revert rollout to previous model variant with a single click/command; include auto-rollback when defined metrics breach.
- Minimal experiment: Implement on staging with simulated metric breach tests; invite one customer to try.

7) Embedded eval snippets in Console (Impact: L / Effort: L)
- Quote: "Hard to validate prompt edits without leaving console." — PM at mid-market company
- Micro-proposal: Add a compact prompt editor that runs your prompt against a small sample dataset (sanitized) and shows diff to baseline.
- Minimal experiment: Prototype in React, ship feature flag to 10 teams.

Prioritization matrix (quick) — H/M/L = high/med/low:
- Cost fingerprinting: H/M
- Predictive fallback: H/H
- Prompt-set alerts: M/M
- Recommendations: M/L
- Latency heatmap: M/M
- Rollback hooks: H/M
- Console eval snippets: L/L

Execution sketches (mini-architectures)
- Cost fingerprinting: small metadata pipeline (publishers at request time) -> daily aggregator -> anomaly detector (simple z-score) -> CSV/Console widget. Keep raw prompts hashed and salted.
- Predictive fallback: sliding-window latency profiler per model-instance + policy engine implementing threshold rules + traffic mirror for safe testing.
- Prompt quality alerts: store small eval-set in customer folder, nightly batch scoring + regression detector, integrate webhook to PagerDuty/Console.

Compliance / privacy considerations:
- Never persist raw customer content for cost fingerprinting; only hashed prompt templates + feature tags.
- Provide opt-out toggle per org for any additional capture.

Owners, near-term plan, and asks to Eng/Product:
- Owner (CS): Leah Kim (this doc).
- Engineering contact: Evan Cole (platform), Marcus Ng (serving-runtime).
- Product partner: Sofia Patel (hosted-api).
- Immediate asks: 1) infra feasibility check for per-request metadata capture (Evan), 2) rough effort estimate for fallback policy engine (Marcus), 3) product validation call script for top 10 customers (Sofia + CS).
- Proposed timeline: 2-week discovery -> 4-week small-bet engineering for 1/2 lanes (cost fingerprinting + rollback hooks) -> pilot 4 weeks. Total MVP ~10–12 weeks to pilot.

Open questions & notes-to-self:
- Q1: How much cardinality can the metadata pipeline tolerate? (user-ids, route names, prompt-template tags)
- Q2: What are SLO impacts if predictive fallback becomes common? Need SRE input.
- Q3: Should prompt-sets live in Console or be API-only? (both have UX and security tradeoffs)
- Note: Connect with legal for data retention policy before beta.

Appendix: sample customer quotes (anonymized)
- "We turned on batching and saw interactions time out more often — trying to find the sweet spot." — e-comm startup
- "A model switch last month changed entity extraction and broke our downstream mapping." — healthcare partner
- "If you give us a daily CSV that explains spend by feature flag, we can do our own analysis." — fintech customer

Next steps (this week):
- Send this doc to Evan/Marcus/Sofia with 1:1 asks (by EOD Fri).
- Draft a short email template for the 10-customer validation call.
- Prepare a 2-slide pitch for Eng All-Hands next Tue (focus: two pilot lanes + risks).

(End of notes)
